A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MedOmniKB and Source Planning Optimisation research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original medical QA experiments, expert evaluations, ablations, and cost measurements, including Tables 4–10 and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds source-transfer experiments, response-uncertainty measurements, and planning statistics.

M1.justification: The exploration, gold-answer-based judging, positive/negative plan construction, and SFT-then-DPO procedure remain unchanged. Source withholding and negative-plan-only training are added experimental variants, not revisions to the proposed SPO method.

E1.justification: The same 11 datasets and MedOmniKB sources are retained. Section 5.8 adds a distinct source-transfer scenario: MedQA, PubMedQA, and SEER are tested using only Book, Research, and Guideline, respectively, including when that source was excluded during training.

E2.justification: v3 adds the explicitly named SPO (OOD corpus) comparison variant in Table 8 and a negative-plan-only SFT control in Table 10. The main benchmark baselines and human-evaluated LLM judge lineup remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols exclude one source from training prompts and labels before testing exclusively on it, introduce negative-plan-only SFT, and evaluate LUQ alongside accuracy. Existing dataset splits, retrieval settings, model configurations, and principal training hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends robustness and diagnostic analysis through source-transfer testing (Section 5.8), response uncertainty with a negative-plan training control (Appendix A.3), and query-length and semantic-diversity comparisons (Appendix B.2). Earlier source-removal, training-stage, data-quantity, and dataset-transfer analyses and case studies remain.

E5.justification: Appendix A.3 newly reports LUQ uncertainty using nine response samples at temperature 0.7, with accuracy evaluated at temperature zero. This introduces a focused uncertainty-estimation procedure; it does not report repeated training runs or confidence intervals for the main benchmark results.

E6.justification: New findings cover source transfer, uncertainty, negative-plan training, and query statistics (Tables 8, 10, 12–13). For example, the new MedQA single-source test reports 65.44 accuracy for SPO (OOD corpus), 62.77 for Frozen, and 69.21 for SPO. These substantially broaden the findings; all original result tables and quantitative plots retain their contents.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, SFT/DPO equations (1–4), and query-diversity definition (5) are unchanged. LUQ is introduced as an empirical evaluation method without new mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, three listed contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about MedOmniKB, source alignment through SPO, and the optimized small planner outperforming larger alternatives. The added experiments support the existing contribution scope.

C2.justification: v3 attributes source transfer to shared medical semantics, interprets lower query diversity as focused retrieval, and links negative-plan uncertainty to the judge recognizing ambiguity. Appendix B.3 also newly argues that low inference costs support real-time use. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the placeholder release address with a concrete project-repository address and identifies long-form evaluators as graduate medical researchers in Shanghai participating voluntarily without special payment. It also discloses that the public knowledge corpora were not anonymized. These are documentation additions, not established changes to existing experiments.

R1.justification: Seven cited works are added, including LUQ, MedS3, EvolveBench, and additional introductory references. The substantive related-work discussion and positioning of SPO against earlier query-construction and source-selection approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language and prompt edits, adds acknowledgements, separates additional analyses into Appendix B, and groups former detail appendices under D.1–D.4. The main narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds four tables, replaces Figure 2's bulimia illustration with an infant dermatitis example, and relocates several appendix displays. Existing quantitative figures and table designs are preserved, with limited caption edits and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The added source-transfer and negative-plan uncertainty experiments strengthen validation beyond v2's existing ablations, while evaluator and access disclosures improve transparency. These are targeted gains with unchanged headline results. A qualification remains: the new real-time suitability assertion relies on cost measurements that exclude reader response generation (Table 11), so deployment implications are only partially supported.
